title: Day 688 — Sheinbaum Unveils "Olinia de Carga" Electric Cargo Vehicle
detail: On August 20, 2026 (Day 688, Thursday), President Sheinbaum unveiled "Olinia de Carga" in the Palacio Nacional courtyard — the second Olinia electric vehicle after the passenger model presented June 7, 2026. The cargo version carries up to 650 kg (up to 12 stackable huacal crates), was engineered by roughly 70 specialists based in Puebla through Mexico's public universities, and is projected to sell for about 150,000 pesos by late 2027. Production will use mixed public-private investment; a public bidding process opens in late September 2026 with formal offers due in November, targeting initial output of 10,000 units per year scaling toward 50,000 per year.

media.caption: Sheinbaum presents "Olinia de Carga," Mexico's electric cargo vehicle, in the Palacio Nacional courtyard

title: Day 688 — Michoacán CJNG Operation Toll Rises to 12 Detained; Tío Lako Still at Large
detail: On August 20, 2026 (Day 688, Thursday), authorities raised the toll from the prior day's federal operation against Tío Lako's CJNG cell in Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán to 12 people detained — his daughter, partner and 10 others — while Tío Lako (Heraclio Guerrero Martínez) himself remained at large. SEDENA, the National Guard, SSPC and the Navy jointly carried out the raids, seizing 64 vehicles (one armored), a .50-caliber machine gun, four 5.56mm mini machine guns, nine long rifles, a handgun, grenade-launcher attachments, eight improvised explosive devices, a drone and ammunition. Officials again linked the crackdown to Tío Lako's alleged orders to attack National Guard troops after the February 22, 2026 SEDENA operation in Tapalpa, Jalisco that killed CJNG leader Rubén "El Mencho" Oseguera Cervantes and Tío Lako's son, Rubén "El R1" Guerrero Valadez.

media.caption: Federal operation against Tío Lako's CJNG cell in Michoacán rises to 12 detained
